column1: # Metro rules: towns shown as their city (final architecture: Q5 = the metro, the whole city).
# rule admin2:<GeoNames country>.<admin1 code>.<admin2 code> with km: every town of that GeoNames second-order division
# within km of the metro is shown as `metro` (a Tokyo special ward: the app's WardCity table; GeoNames' admin2 code is
# the ward's geonameid). A town of the division farther out fails the build (a misplaced record: drop it in
# places-overrides.tsv); check_name is the ward's name: every town of the metro's prefecture with that name must be
# folded, and towns of that name elsewhere with 100,000 people or more are listed in the build report for review.
# rule admin1:<GeoNames country>.<admin1 code> with km: every town of that first-order division within km of the metro
# is shown as the metro (a city-province's districts: Istanbul, Mexico City); separate towns farther out keep their
# names. check_name: the metro's English name.
# rule place:<geonameid>: one town is shown as `metro`.
# Sections of a city (GeoNames PPLX) need no row: each folds into its GeoNames municipality's seat within 15 km,
# else the nearest larger non-section town within 15 km of the same country.
# Tokyo: the 23 special wards; the Tama cities (Hachioji, Machida, Fuchu, Chofu...) stay themselves (golden points pin
# both). No regions-bundle district outline is read (those are geoBoundaries, CC BY-SA: LICENSES.md).
